definition: Decomposing an image into semantic and geometric structure — objects, regions, layout — a comprehensive scene-understanding task.
details: Decomposing an image into semantic and geometric structure — objects, regions, layout — a comprehensive scene-understanding task.

explainer.lead: Scene parsing breaks an image into labelled regions and layout, covering objects, surfaces, and structure together. It matters because downstream decisions need the whole scene, not just isolated detections.

tiers.eli5: It's like taking a photo apart into labelled pieces — sky here, road there, car here — so a computer knows what everything is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for dense per-pixel labelling feeding navigation and editing pipelines; a pitfall is that rare classes and boundary pixels are poorly handled, so fine edges blur.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it assigns a class label to every pixel, c in C, over the image grid, often trained with per-pixel cross-entropy. Limits: strong class imbalance and ambiguous boundaries degrade accuracy on small or thin structures.

explainer.example: An urban street photo is labelled pixel-wise as road, sidewalk, building, sky, and pedestrian.
